key.description: What format agent definitions use. Varies widely: Markdown with YAML frontmatter, JSON config files, TOML sections, or AGENTS.md plain markdown.

definition_format.mechanism: markdown files with YAML frontmatter (name, description, tools, mcpServers fields) documented under 'YAML frontmatter properties' heading

key.description: Whether agents can have their own MCP server configuration, scoping which external tools each agent can access.

per_agent_mcp.mechanism: per-agent mcpServers section in YAML frontmatter scopes which MCP servers each agent can access, documented under 'MCP server configuration details' / 'MCP server configurations' headings

key.description: Whether agents can be restricted to specific tools via allowlists, denylists, tool categories, or per-tool configuration maps.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-AGENT §9.1 (DERIVABLE); tool vocabulary ACIF-CORE Appendix A

tool_restrictions.mechanism: per-agent tool allowlist via tools field, with tool aliases for renaming, documented under 'Tools' / 'Tool aliases' / 'Tools processing' headings

key.description: What kinds of executors hooks support beyond shell commands. May include HTTP endpoints, LLM prompt evaluation, multi-turn agent handlers, or TypeScript extensions.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-HOOK §10.1 (DERIVABLE); handler-type enum ACIF-HOOK Appendix B, §8.2

handler_types.mechanism: hook handler types documented under 'Hook types' heading (session, prompt, tool, error)

key.description: Whether hooks communicate with the host via structured JSON on stdin/stdout rather than plain text or exit codes alone.

json_io_protocol.mechanism: JSON I/O protocol documented under 'Reading input' / 'Outputting JSON' headings

always.mechanism: .github/copilot-instructions.md applies to all requests in repository scope (documented under 'Repository-wide custom instructions')

glob.mechanism: NAME.instructions.md uses 'applyTo' frontmatter glob to scope to file patterns (documented under 'Path-specific custom instructions')

key.description: How rules decide when to load into context. Providers implement varying modes: always-on, conditional/glob-based, model-decision, and manual activation. Tracks which modes the provider supports and how they are configured.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-RULE §9.1 (DERIVABLE); activation-mode vocabulary ACIF-RULE Appendix A, §10

agents_md.mechanism: AGENTS.md at repository root, cwd, or COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS (documented under 'Agent instructions' section)

claude_md.mechanism: CLAUDE.md at repository root recognized alongside AGENTS.md (documented under 'Agent instructions' section)

gemini_md.mechanism: GEMINI.md at repository root recognized alongside AGENTS.md (documented under 'Agent instructions' section)

key.description: Which rule file formats from other providers this provider recognizes. Contents: recognized_formats (list of filenames like AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules). Minimum qualification: supported when the provider reads at least one rule-file format defined by a different provider.
Whether rules load from multiple directory levels with defined precedence. Enables project-root rules plus subdirectory-scoped overrides.

hierarchical_loading.mechanism: four-tier scope: Repository-wide + Path-specific + Agent (AGENTS.md) + Local ($HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md) — files merge across tiers (documented under 'Repository-wide' / 'Path-specific' / 'Agent instructions' / 'Local instructions')

key.description: The required or conventional filename for this skill type. For example, "SKILL.md" for Claude Code skills.
Whether the skill can be installed at global/personal scope (applies across all projects for the current user).
Whether the skill can be installed at project scope (applies to current project only, typically committed to version control).

project_scope.mechanism: skill directory under .github/skills/<name>/, .claude/skills/<name>/, or .agents/skills/<name>/ in project repository

skills.cli_management.mechanism: skill management commands documented under 'Skills commands in the CLI' heading
